positive_findings: authority() reloads local_env.md and checks config SHA, gz02 host, exact project/UI paths and forbidden container policy before transport; inherited NANHAI_* values are ignored.

stage_once() creates fsynced UNKNOWN.json with O_EXCL before injected transport; a second call cannot retry. TERMINAL.json is separate, and timeout/parse/write failures preserve UNKNOWN for read-only reconciliation.
Remote program walks symlink-free directory fds, checks project/control UID, source SHA/bytes/mode, target UID/size/mode/SHA and stable readback, and never overwrites a differing final path.
Ten recorded local fixtures cover authority, one-shot receipts, timeout, terminal write failure, symlink control and a replacement occurring before cleanup's inode check.
CLI --stage returns rc3 before SSH; no runner, graph, container, namespace or device command is exposed.
remaining_risks: conditional_unlink() calls os.stat(name) and then os.unlink(name); replacement between those two syscalls could still cause deletion of another inode. The fixture injects replacement before os.stat, so it does not close this race.

check_chain() reopens and compares parent fds before/after mutation, but the named path can change between check and os.link/os.unlink. Such drift becomes uncertain and may leave a residual file; it is not an atomic path binding.
UNKNOWN can remain after a failed terminal receipt as designed; reconcile remote final and partial names read-only before any future attempt.
minimum_repair: Do not automatically unlink a final pathname after uncertain readback or cleanup. Preserve UNKNOWN and reconcile; if cleanup is required, use an externally exclusive owner/lock protocol covering directory mutation and prove it in a race fixture. Treat parent-path drift the same way.
scope: Static protocol review only. v6 runner --run is itself hard-closed rc3; staging its bytes would not authorize a graph. Peer executed no SSH, staging, runner, graph, container or device action.
